lecture_title: Black Holes, White Holes, and the Global Causal Diagram

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The time rescaling and complete near-horizon Rindler metric are legible together, with no obstruction over the equations.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Now, this is the metric close to the black hole horizon.
assets.caption_hint: Near-horizon metric and dimensionless Schwarzschild time

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The polar metric, asymptotic constant coefficient, cigar profile, and circumference scale are simultaneously visible without lecturer occlusion.
assets.caption_hint: Euclidean cigar interpolation and asymptotic circumference

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The accumulated diagram preserves both null horizons, future and past singularity curves, and the colored observer trajectories; the central causal structure remains visible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: We are going to talk about Penrose diagrams.
assets.caption_hint: Uncompactified black-hole and white-hole causal structure

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The completed radial Minkowski compactification grid is visible with its finite triangle, crowded constant-coordinate curves, and endpoint labels.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: What about a black hole? What does a black hole look like?
assets.caption_hint: Completed Penrose diagram for radial Minkowski spacetime

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The completed eternal Schwarzschild diagram is unobstructed and shows singularities, horizons, null trajectories, the second exterior, and the asymptotic boundary.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That is the Schwarzschild black hole in a nutshell, drawn all of spacetime on a finite piece of a plane.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The shell is drawn as a clear circle with the Minkowski metric inside and Schwarzschild labeled outside, directly matching the Birkhoff-theorem statement.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: We piece together two things, both of which we know very well, connected together by a shell.
assets.caption_hint: Flat interior and Schwarzschild exterior of a spherical shell
